issue.title: Future-Pomodoro-link cleanup leaves a dangling trailing newline when the pruned bullet is the file's last line
issue.description:
Discovered while implementing the plan activate_future_scheduled_pomodoro_links.md
(bob-plugins repo, plugins/block-id-prompt/main.js).

listItemSubtreeEdit() (used by planFuturePomodoroLinkCleanup(), called from
completeTaskSourceLink() to prune duplicate future-Pomodoro links) computes the removed
span as [start-of-removed-line, start-of-next-line-or-content.length). This correctly
merges surrounding content when the removed bullet is in the middle of the file, but
when the removed bullet IS the file's last line (no trailing newline after it), the
newline that separated it from the PREVIOUS line is left untouched and nothing follows
to reconnect to, so the file gains a trailing newline it never had.

Repro: a note ending in (no trailing newline)
  - [ ] Later ()
    - [[Alpha#^ship]]
where "[[Alpha#^ship]]" is a dedicated duplicate-link bullet that
planFuturePomodoroLinkCleanup prunes as part of completing a task-picker link elsewhere
in the same Pomodoros section. After pruning, the file ends with
"- [ ] Later ()\n" instead of "- [ ] Later ()" — an unwanted trailing newline introduced
by the cleanup edit.

I worked around this in my own new tests (scripts/test-block-id-prompt.cjs) by ensuring
the pruned bullet is never literally the last line of the fixture, so it did not block
the plan I was implementing. The same subtree-removal shape may exist elsewhere in this
monorepo (e.g. bob-navigation-hotkeys/main.js shares similar list-subtree-removal
helpers) — worth checking during triage whether the same bug is present there too.
